CLAREMONT CITY COUNCIL
  MEETING AGENDA
  “We are a vibrant, livable, and inclusive community dedicated to quality services,
  safety, financial strength, sustainability, preservation, and progress
  with equal representation for our community.”

City Council Chamber  Tuesday
225 Second Street  September 26, 2023
Claremont, CA 91711
  5:15 PM

  COUNCILMEMBERS

  ED REECE
  MAYOR

  COREY CALAYCAY  JENNIFER STARK  SAL MEDINA  JED LEANO

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a special meeting of the City Council of the
City of Claremont, California, as called by the City Council of the City of
Claremont, will be held on the 26th day of September 2023 at 5:15 p.m. at the
above location for the purpose of considering the items listed below. The
Brown Act provides for an opportunity for members of the public to address
the City Council concerning the items described below. Each speaker will be
limited to three (3) continuous minutes.

Meetings are open to the public for in-person attendance or remotely via Zoom. Should Zoom be
disrupted, the in-person meeting will continue unless one or more Councilmembers are attending the
meeting remotely pursuant to Assembly Bill 2449.

To participate in the meeting via Zoom, download Zoom on any phone or computer device. Cut and
paste the following link into your browser to access and participate in the live City Council meeting at
5:15 p.m.: https://zoom.us/j/256208090 or to only listen from the phone dial (213)338-8477, Webinar ID:
256 208 090. The recorded meeting will be uploaded to the City website and archived.

Public comment may be provided by one of the following methods. Each speaker will be given up to
three (3) minutes to provide their comment.

OPTION 1: IN-PERSON LIVE COMMENTS – When the item you wish to speak to is announced, please
proceed to the speaker’s podium one by one.

OPTION 2: REMOTE LIVE COMMENTS – Through Zoom, if you wish to speak, you may virtually select
the "raise hand" button. If you are dialing in by telephone and wish to speak, please enter *9.
 Page 2  City Council Agenda  September 26, 2023

OPTION 3: E-MAIL/MAIL – Written comments sent to the City Clerk’s office will be distributed to the City
Council and imaged into the record of the meeting. Email: sdesautels@ci.claremont.ca.us,
jcostanza@ci.claremont.ca.us. Mail: PO Box 880, Claremont, CA 91711. Written comments submitted
after publication of the agenda will be made available in the document archive system on the City
website as soon as possible - www.ci.claremont.ca.us.

OPTION 4: BY TELEPHONE – Members of the public wanting to address the City Council via telephone
are requested to inform the City Clerk's office no later than 3:00 p.m. by calling either (909) 399-5461 or
(909) 399-5463. You will be called during consideration of the item you are interested in.

CALL TO ORDER THE MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL

REMOTE PARTICIPATION REQUEST PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 2449
If a member of the legislative body is attending pursuant to Assembly Bill 2449 and Zoom is
disrupted, the meeting will be suspended until Zoom can be restored.

CLOSED SESSION

The City Council will recess to closed session:

1. Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54956.8:

  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATORS
  Property: Vacant Lot – SE 1/4 of SE 1/4 (EX T/L EASE AND EX WEBB CANYON DEBRIS
  DISPOSAL AREA) (PER F M 20291-1) OF SEC 29 T 1N R 8W
  Agency negotiator: City Manager Adam Pirrie
  Negotiating parties: County of Los Angeles Tax Collector, Richard Seaver, and Byron
  Seaver
  Under negotiation: Price and terms of payment

and

2. Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and (e)(3):

  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Significant exposure to litigation pursuant to paragraph (2) of subdivision (d) and paragraph
  (3) of subdivision (e) of Section 54956.9: One Potential Case
  On behalf of Cari McCormick and a class of similarly situated persons, Aiman-Smith &
  Marcy has submitted a claim to the California Public Employees Retirement System
  (CalPERS), the State of California, and the County of Lake alleging age discrimination in
  CalPERS’s method of calculating certain disability retirement benefits. The claim lists every
  governmental agency that offers CalPERS retirement benefits to their employees as a
  potential defendant, including the City of Claremont.

ADJOURNMENT

THE NEXT REGULAR MEETING OF THE CLAREMONT CITY COUNCIL WILL BE HELD ON,
SEPTEMBER 26, 2023, AT 6:30 P.M., IN THE CLAREMONT COUNCIL CHAMBER, 225 WEST
SECOND STREET, CLAREMONT, CA 91711.
 Page 3  City Council Agenda  September 26, 2023

IN COMPLIANCE WITH THE AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT 0F 1990, THIS AGENDA WILL
BE MADE AVAILABLE IN APPROPRIATE ALTERNATIVE FORMATS TO PERSONS WITH
DISABILITIES. ANY PERSON WITH A DISABILITY WHO REQUIRES A MODIFICATION OR
ACCOMMODATION IN ORDER TO PARTICIPATE IN A CITY MEETING SHOULD CONTACT THE
CITY CLERK AT 909-399-5461 “VOICE” OR 1-800-735-2929 “TT/TTY” AT LEAST THREE (3)
WORKING DAYS PRIOR TO THE MEETING, IF POSSIBLE.

I, SHELLEY DESAUTELS, CITY CLERK OF THE CITY OF CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, HEREBY
CERTIFY UNDER PENALTY OF PERJURY THAT THE FOREGOING AGENDA WAS POSTED AT
CLAREMONT CITY HALL, 207 HARVARD AVENUE, ON  SEPTEMBER 21, 2023, PURSUANT TO
GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 56456.

POST THROUGH: September 27, 2023
